name: toilet safety frame
definition: free-standing or toilet-fixed frame with armrests round a toilet that helps a person sit down and rise.
reason: Drive and Binsons sell 'toilet safety frames' apart from raised seats and grab bars; frame form no kind covers.

name: bath lift
definition: powered seat that lowers a person into the bath and raises them out again.
reason: Drive sells 'bath lifts' as own category; powered lowering seat differs in form from a shower chair.

name: tub transfer bench
definition: bench that straddles the bath wall so a person sits outside the bath and slides across into it.
reason: Drive lists 'transfer benches' apart from bath benches and stools; made for transfer, not only sitting to wash.

name: bed rail
definition: rail or assist handle fitted to a bed to prevent falls or help a person sit up and stand.
reason: Invacare sells bed rails; fits any home bed, so not an H2.12 part; bed-care leaf.

name: manual blood-pressure kit
definition: gauge with arm cuff and hand bulb, read by listening with a stethoscope (aneroid sphygmomanometer, with or without stethoscope).
reason: Needs a stethoscope and skill; form and use differ from automatic monitors (C10 b). Logged page does not show it: HV_NK attests.

name: peak flow meter
definition: handheld tube with a scale that measures how fast a person can breathe out, used to monitor asthma.
reason: Every monitor is H2.1 (H-9); no leaf measures lung function, so new leaf H2.1.9. No logged page shows it: HV_NK attests.

name: HbA1c home test kit
definition: one-use kit that measures average blood glucose (HbA1c) from a fingerstick blood sample.
reason: Measures its own quantity; not a meter or strip; tests are H2.1 (H-9). No logged page shows it: HV_NK attests.

name: steam inhaler
definition: device that makes warm steam to be breathed in for cold, cough or sinus relief, without liquid medicine.
reason: Steam, not a medicine mist, so the nebuliser definition fails. Harvester saw Beurer SI30; logged summary omits it: HV_NK attests.

name: penile traction device
definition: device that stretches the penis, sold with a stated medical purpose such as Peyronie's disease or length after surgery.
reason: Osbon sells RestoreX traction kit beside vacuum devices; medical purpose stated, so H2.2.4 (K-33), not H3.

name: mobility vehicle lift
definition: powered lift fitted inside a car or on its hitch that raises a mobility scooter or wheelchair into or onto the vehicle.
reason: Scooter Direct sells 'mobility lifts' as own category; access aid like a ramp, made for any scooter, not one model.

name: electronic magnifier
definition: camera-and-screen device, handheld or desktop, that enlarges print and images for a low-vision user (video magnifier, CCTV).
reason: Camera and screen change the form (C10 b) from optical magnifiers. Harvester saw a nav link only: HV_NK attests.

name: low-vision monocular
definition: small handheld telescope made and sold as a low-vision aid for seeing at a distance.
reason: Keplerian telescopes sold among low-vision aids; held, not in a frame (low-vision spectacles), K-38 home by sale as aid.

name: eye-gaze access device
definition: eye tracker fixed to a computer or tablet so a person with little movement can control it and communicate by gaze.
reason: PCEye is an input camera bar, not a speech device; Tobii Dynavox sells it beside its SGDs as its own type.

name: fat burner

reason: Sold in sports-nutrition ranges as its own type; role differs from pre-workout. Logged summary omits it: HV_NK attests.

name: protein snack
definition: snack other than a bar (chips, crisps, cookies) sold for its protein.
reason: Quest sells protein chips beside bars; a different product compared on its own. Logged summary omits it: HV_NK attests.

name: tubular bandage
definition: elastic or gauze tube pulled over a limb to support it or hold a dressing.
reason: Tube, not a roll or triangle: form of supply differs (leaf axis); Tubigrip sold as its own type.

name: blister plaster
definition: hydrocolloid cushion plaster made to protect and heal a blister.
reason: Galaxus guide separates blister plasters (Compeed) from strips; hydrocolloid pad differs from an adhesive bandage.

name: corn and callus remover
definition: medicated plaster, pad or liquid (for example salicylic acid) labelled to remove corns or calluses.
reason: Medicated, so a medicine by labelled use (H-2); no skin or foot use class, so new leaf H2.6.9. Unmedicated corn cushions: H1.

name: wound-closure strip
definition: thin adhesive strips that hold the edges of a cut together while it heals.
reason: Steri-Strip closes a wound rather than covering it; sold under its own name; form of supply differs.

name: heat patch sold for pain
definition: self-heating patch stuck on the body and sold to relieve muscle or joint pain.
reason: Pain claim makes it H2 (K-31; H1 heat pack has none); heat therapy, so pain leaf. Capsaicin plaster is a medicine, H2.6.3.

name: liquid bandage
definition: spray or liquid that dries to a protective film over a small wound.
reason: Galaxus lists spray plaster as its own type; liquid film is a different form of supply.

name: contact-lens rewetting drops
definition: drops put in the eye with lenses in place to rewet and soothe them.
reason: Used in the eye, not to clean or store lenses, so the solution definition fails. Logged summary omits it: HV_NK attests.
